newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-LEHMANN HITS HIS FIRST CENTURY FOR YORKSHIRE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LEHMANN HITS HIS FIRST CENTURY FOR YORKSHIRE.

text.p: Australian Darren Lehmann struck his first century for Yorkshire on Thursday in his debut season on the English county circuit.
The South Australian batsman made an unbeaten 109 against Somerset on the second day of the rain-hit four-day championship match at Taunton.
Lehmann's century propped up Yorkshire, who were 52 for three overnight and slipped to 122 for five in gloomy conditions before they recovered to 183 for five at the close.
Having reached his half-century in two hours, Lehmann needed a further 83 minutes to reach three figures, having faced 168 balls and with 13 boundaries.
A savage square drive proved particularly productive, and when a scampered single brought up his 100, Lehmann raised both arms to salute the Yorkshire balcony and punched the air several times.
Essex left-arm paceman Mark Ilott grabbed four for 17, including two wickets with consecutive deliveries, to rock championship leaders Gloucestershire at Gloucester.
Gloucestershire were reeling on 84 for seven at the end of a rain-shortened second day after the first day had been washed out.
Former England captain Graham Gooch held two slip catches to help give Essex the initiative, then Ilott returned for a second a spell to dispatch Mark Alleyne and Richard Davis with successive balls.
Derbyshire's England discard Devon Malcolm continued to press his claim for an international recall with four for 42 against Nottinghamshire at Trent Bridge.
Malcolm, the country's leading early-season wicket-taker, started with a three-wicket burst in which he also broke a finger on opener Paul Pollard's left hand.
Notts slumped to 128 for eight in the face of Derbyshire's 319 but avoided the follow-on thanks to Usman Afzaal, who hit 52, his third successive half-century.
Notts finished with 192 -- 127 behind -- and reduced Derbyshire to six for one in their second innings at the close.
Off-spinner Adrian Pierson snapped up four for 42 in 28 overs to give champions Leicestershire the upper hand against Surrey at Leicester.
Opener Mark Butcher with 59 off 86 balls offered the main resistance as Surrey struggled to 235 for eight on the second day after rain prevented any play on the first.
